description:
Define formal schemas for the four .agent/ configuration files declared in
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2, plus the .agent/version integer (§10). Implement
in Rust (this repo is a Cargo project — see Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs) as serde
structs, with schemars-derived JSON schemas exported to `schemas/` for
external tooling.

=== What to build ===

One load-and-validate function per config: reads file, parses via serde_yaml,
applies cross-field validation, returns a typed result with precise errors.
No runtime harness behavior. No dispatch. Just parse, validate, expose typed
config.

=== Shapes from ARCHITECTURE.md ===

providers.yaml (§4.1, §4.2) — "provider" used strictly in the inference-
provider sense (endpoint + auth pair; see §4.1 cross-ref to TAXONOMY.md §2):

    providers:
      <name>:
        endpoint: <url>
        auth:
          type: api_key | aws_sigv4 | ...
          env: <var-name>         # for api_key
          profile: <aws-profile>  # for aws_sigv4
    models:
      <name>:
        provider: <provider-name>
        model_id: <id>
        capabilities: [tool_use_native, prompt_caching, streaming, stop_sequences, ...]
        context_window: <int>

Decision: does `models:` live in providers.yaml or its own models.yaml?
Arch doesn't commit. Recommend same file — providers and their models belong
together. Flag in the implementing task's commit message if you split them.

Capabilities are extend-only (§4.2): once declared, names stay in the
registry. Seed with those named in the arch; warn (don't fail) on unknown
names so models from new providers can declare new capabilities without
blocking.

agents.yaml (§4.3):

    agents:
      <role>:
        model: <model-name>        # must resolve to a defined model
        system_prompt: <path>      # relative to .agent/system/

Minimum known roles referenced in the arch: worker, compactor, verifier.

manifest.yaml (§5.1):

    context:
      pinned:        [paths — always included]
      include:       [globs — ordered inclusion]
      budget_tokens: <int>
      overflow:      drop_oldest_exchanges | truncate_oldest | summarize | drop

workflow.yaml (§6) — declarative, data-first; avoid Turing-completeness:

    events:
      <event-name>:
        - <action-expression>

Events seen in arch examples: user_message, worker_return, verifier_approve,
verifier_reject, branch_stopped. Actions: spawn_exchange, dispatch(<role>),
dispatch(<role>, with: <data>), gate_merge_on(<predicate>), merge,
mark_abandoned, notify_ui. Define the closed set in the schema; extending
it is a code change, intentionally.

.agent/version (§10): a bare integer. Start at 1. Migration code is written
when it bumps.

=== Cross-field validation to enforce at load ===

- agents.*.model must resolve to a defined model.
- models.*.provider must resolve to a defined provider.
- models.*.capabilities: warn on names outside the registry; don't fail.
- manifest.pinned / manifest.include: path-shape sanity; don't hard-fail
  on non-existence since some paths (e.g. .agent/goal.md) are written at
  dispatch time.
- workflow events must be drawn from the known event set; actions must
  be known action names with correct arity.

=== Deliverables ===

1. Rust serde structs + schemars derives for each YAML, under src/config/
   or similar. Keep the crate scope narrow.
2. Per-config load-and-validate entry point returning Result<Config, LoadError>
   with errors that name the file, the key, and the problem.
3. Generated JSON schemas written to `schemas/*.json` via a `make schemas`
   target. Useful for editor integration and for the template task's
   validation pass.
4. Unit tests: round-trip parse of every YAML example appearing in
   ARCHITECTURE.md; each cross-field validation failure mode; error
   message quality (snapshot or substring assertions).
5. If any shape decision diverges from ARCHITECTURE.md examples (e.g.
   where models: lives), update ARCHITECTURE.md in the same task.

=== Constraints ===

- Parse+validate only. No HTTP, no provider dispatch, no runtime state.
- Terminology: every schema field name and example must conform to
  ARCHITECTURE.md §2.1. No "turn", no bare "call", no "session".
- Coverage: 100% on new code per repo policy (Makefile runs tarpaulin in
  pre-commit).

=== References ===

- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2 (directory layout), §4.1–§4.3 (providers/models/
  agents), §5.1 (manifest), §6 (workflow), §10 (version).
- docs/TAXONOMY.md §2 (provider disambiguation), §4 (tool/skill distinction).
- AGENTS.md (terminology discipline; tests/docs/alignment gates required).
title: Config schemas: manifest, workflow, providers, agents
